scenarios.title: Pinch only with the declared cover
scenarios.objective: Evaluate a pinch under an explicitly stated cover assignment.
scenarios.briefing: Navy uses a drill rule: YOU may pinch the puck-side wall only while F3 covers your high position. F1 contests Gold 1’s rim; F3 is currently closer to Gold’s net than the puck, so the named cover is not established. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: F3 is deeper in the attacking zone than YOU, rather than occupying the high position.

questions.prompt: Is the stated high cover already established?

options.text: Whether F3 can establish the agreed cover

questions.prompt: Arrange a supported-pinch decision.

options.text: Read the wall contest
Confirm the assigned high cover
Pinch or recover based on the updated picture

questions.explanation: The checks may overlap. Do not treat this drill’s cover rule as every team’s system.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a conservative high position while cover is uncertain.
questions.explanation: The reference retains access to central recovery rather than committing to the wall. Other high positions may work.

questions.prompt: F3 now reaches your vacated point and calls the switch. What changes?

options.text: The cover condition is met, but the puck contest still needs checking
The pinch becomes certain to win
Gold 1 no longer affects the decision

questions.explanation: A covered pinch can still lose a race or encounter a closed route.

questions.prompt: Explain what makes this a supported pinch rather than simply an aggressive move.
questions.explanation: Identify F3’s actual coverage, D2’s position and the puck situation; do not rely on the word “pinch” alone.

questions.prompt: F3 has not reached YOUR high position. Which call fits before a possible pinch?

options.text: F3, confirm high cover before I step down
D2 is on the ice, so I am going now
F1 is near the puck, so the cover can wait

questions.explanation: The drill names F3 as the replacement for YOUR high position. Ask for that cover and check the puck route before committing; a call alone does not establish it.

questions.prompt: After F3 reaches high cover, which changes would make YOU reconsider the pinch?

options.text: F3 leaves that high position
The puck moves beyond F1’s reachable route
Gold stays away from the puck

questions.explanation: The hypothetical cover is now established, but a change in cover or puck access can remove the reason to pinch. Hold or recover if the updated picture no longer supports it.

questions.prompt: Move F3 to illustrate the named replacement for YOUR high position.
questions.explanation: F3 is now near YOUR high area, on the neutral-zone side of the wall contest. This illustrates the cover condition; whether a pinch is reachable still needs a fresh puck read.

questions.prompt: F3 reaches YOUR high area, but the loose puck travels past F1 toward neutral ice. What changes?
questions.explanation: High cover satisfies only one condition. If YOU cannot reach the puck safely, hold or recover and communicate the escape route. F3 arriving does not make every pinch useful.
